summary: Backend (12/12 pytest) and frontend pages all load. CRITICAL: Delhivery shipment creation integration is broken - the create.json call returns 'format key missing in POST' from Delhivery, so no waybills are generated and all shipments persist as 'Pending' without a waybill. Root cause: Delhivery's /cmu/create.json endpoint expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded body (format=json&data=<json_string>), but server.py sends it as JSON. Because the HTTP call still returns 200, the backend silently saves a useless shipment record - downstream features (track, label) cannot work.

critical.issue: Delhivery create.json call sends JSON body but the API requires form-encoded body 'format=json&data=<json_str>'. Delhivery returns {success:false, rmk:'format key missing in POST'}, no waybill is returned, but backend still saves shipment (status=Pending, waybill=None). Should either (a) switch to form-encoded request as per Delhivery docs, and (b) raise/return an error to the client when delhivery_response.success is false instead of silently persisting.
Cannot be exercised because no shipment ever gets a waybill (returns 400 'No waybill found'). Blocked by the create bug above.

minor.issue: When Delhivery responds with success=false, backend swallows the failure and stores a Pending shipment. Should check delhivery_response.get('success') and surface the error (rmk) to the caller.

today_shipments query compares ISO string with $gte against a datetime-derived isoformat - works only because created_at is stored as ISO string; fragile if datetime objects are ever stored. Consider storing created_at as native datetime in Mongo.
Simply delegates to receive_order; both endpoints exist but do identical work. Consider de-duplicating or documenting intent.

integration_issues.issue: Form submits, shipment is created in DB but waybill is N/A and status stays Pending due to backend Delhivery integration bug. User has no error feedback - looks like success.

issues: Stats use 4 cards (Today/In Transit/Delivered/Exceptions). Total shipments count from backend is never displayed. Layout, contrast and spacing look clean (Swiss style).

action_items: Fix Delhivery create.json integration: use form-urlencoded POST. Replace httpx call with: client.post(url, data={'format':'json','data': json.dumps(shipment_payload)}, headers={'Authorization': f'Token {API_KEY}'}) (do NOT set Content-Type to application/json).

After Delhivery call, check response['success'] and response['error']; if false, raise HTTPException(400, detail=response.get('rmk','Delhivery rejected order')) instead of persisting a Pending shipment.
Surface backend errors in CreateShipment.jsx UI on submission failure.

Note: Even after the form-encoding fix, shipments may still fail until the pickup_location ('TestWarehouse') is registered with the Delhivery client warehouse setup. Recommend adding a 'register warehouse' helper or clearer error message.
Verify pickup endpoint - it also currently posts JSON to /fm/request/new/; double-check Delhivery docs for the correct content type.

After main agent fixes Delhivery integration to use form-encoded body, re-run pytest and additionally verify: (1) POST /api/orders returns shipment with a non-null waybill and status=Manifested; (2) GET /api/shipments/{id}/track returns tracking data; (3) GET /api/shipments/{id}/label returns a label URL; (4) Frontend CreateShipment shows success/error toast appropriately.
rca of the issue: Delhivery /cmu/create.json requires a form-encoded payload of the shape 'format=json&data=<json string>'. The backend currently sends 'Content-Type: application/json' with a JSON body {'format':'json','data':{...}}. Delhivery does not parse JSON bodies for this endpoint, so its parser does not find the 'format' key and rejects the upload with rmk='format key missing in POST'. Backend currently does not check the success flag in the Delhivery response, so the failed upload is persisted as a Pending shipment without a waybill. Fix: use httpx data= (form-encoded) with json.dumps for the data field; verify response.success; on failure raise HTTPException with rmk message.
